name: The Shrine
summary: A stepped altar crowned with horns of consecration, clay idols with their arms up, and a bronze double axe on its pole.
description: The palace keeps its gods close and its gods keep their offerings closer. A stepped bench altar stands in the corner under a pair of gypsum horns, clay idols lined up along its lower step with their arms raised in the gesture that means either blessing or surrender, and across the room a bronze double axe stands on its pole, the sign of the house, taller than a man. The worshippers sit on low benches at the back and face the altar. The idols are small, light and unlucky; the offering table is usually worth the risk.
build: Shell: the kit's InnerWard shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m painted plaster walls 4.00 m clear, 0.45 m fresco-blue capstone band, an archway 2.60 × 2.88 m centred on every wall.
Procession fresco: a panel 4.10 m wide × 1.40 m tall, 1.60–3.00 m above the floor, on each section of the north, east and west walls, haematite border on top.

Stepped altar (NE): gypsum lower step 2.60 × 0.90 × 0.45 m at (3.80, 5.05) with a haematite band 0.08 m along its front top edge; upper step 1.80 × 0.45 × 0.35 m at (3.80, 5.27) against the north wall.
Horns of consecration: gypsum, 0.80 m across, on the upper step at (3.80, 5.27).
Clay idols: three, 0.45 m tall (a bell skirt r 0.10 → 0.03 m, a head r 0.06 m, arms raised), on the lower step at x 3.00, 3.35, 4.25, y 4.75.
Offering table: a painted table 0.60 × 0.60 m, 0.70 m high, at (3.60, 3.30), before the altar.

Double axe (NW): a stepped gypsum stand 0.80 × 0.80 × 0.30 m and 0.50 × 0.50 × 0.30 m at (−3.80, 4.20); a bronze pole r 0.03 × 1.40 m; the axe head at 2.30 m above ground, two curved blades each 0.45 m long × 0.50 m tall × 0.04 m.
Worshippers' benches: plastered, 3.00 × 0.40 × 0.40 m, three rows each side at x ±3.60, y −2.40, −3.60, −4.80, facing north.
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.88 m (InnerWard), all open
Altar: NE, lower step at 0.75 m above ground

gameplay: The idols are light, quick loot that the household notices missing.
The double axe stand and the altar are the only cover north of the cross; the benches are low cover to the south.
A quiet room: no fire, lit from the archways.
